clean_source_blocks.text: Rebel fighters and Rwandan troops are accused of committing atrocities after capturing the DR Congo city of Uvira in December.

Summary executions and rape were among the atrocities committed by the M23 rebel group and Rwandan soldiers during their weeks-long occupation of the lakeside city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, an investigation by a leading rights group has found. Human Rights Watch (HRW) says its investigators found evidence of the execution of 53 civilians - 46 men, one woman and six children - during door-to-door raids in the city's neighbourhoods after the rebels, widely believed to be backed by Rwanda, captured it in December. Rwanda has consistently denied that it supports that M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to resource-rich eastern DR Congo. But HRW says many of the interviewees alleged witnessing atrocities committed by uniformed Rwandan soldiers as well as M23 fighters.

"They [M23 fighters] shot my neighbour first in the head," said one of the 130 residents interviewed by HRW. Another said he saw four members of his family killed. "I wasn't hit so I just ran to the lake. I saw my brother, his wife, and two of his children fall," he was quoted as saying. The M23 and Rwandan government have not yet responded to a BBC request for comment. Warning: This article contains descriptions of sexual violence The M23 captured Uvira - which lies on the shores of Lake Tanganyika - days after US President Donald Trump brokered a peace deal between DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi and his Rwandan counterpart Paul Kagame in a bid to end the devastating conflict in the resource-rich region.

The US and European powers accuse Rwanda - which borders eastern DR Congo - of supporting the rebel offensive. UN experts have accused Rwanda of having "de facto control" of the M23's operations. They said M23 recruits were trained under Rwandan supervision and supported by high-tech Rwandan weaponry. The M23 withdrew from Uvira - the gateway to Burundi, a key military ally of DR Congo - in January following intense diplomatic pressure. The HRW report is the first detailed study of what happened in the city when it was under M23 control. Tens of thousands of people fled their homes when the group seized control of it. HRW says it documented eight cases of rape allegedly committed by the rebels and Rwandan soldiers during the occupation.

[Lähde: Human Rights Watch]
(Kinshasa) – The M23 armed group and Rwandan military forces carried out an abusive month-long occupation of the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo city of Uvira beginning in December 2025, Human Right Watch said in a report released today.

The 23-page report,“‘We Are Civilians!’: Killings, Sexual Violence, and Abductions by the M23 and Rwandan Forces in Uvira, Democratic Republic of Congo,” documents the M23 and Rwandan forces’ occupation of Uvira, the second largest city in South Kivu province from December 10, 2025, days after the signing of the United States-brokered Washington Accords, until their withdrawal on January 17, 2026. During this time, these forces shot fleeing civilians, summarily executed more than 50 people during door-to-door searches, raped at least 8 women, and forcibly disappeared at least 12 people.

Killings, Sexual Violence, and Abductions by the M23 and Rwandan Forces in Uvira, Democratic Republic of Congo

“After taking control of Uvira, M23 fighters and Rwandan forces went door-to-door to summarily kill men and boys and committed rape and abductions,” said Philippe Bolopion, executive director at Human Rights Watch. “Human Rights Watch documented numerous horrific abuses but may have only scratched the surface. Criminal investigations are needed, including by the International Criminal Court, to ensure these crimes do not go unpunished.”

The report, the result of the first field research into abuses in Uvira during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, is based on over 120 interviews conducted in March and April 2026. Human Rights Watch wrote to the government of Rwanda and to Bertrand Bisimwa, the head of the M23, to provide the report’s preliminary findings, but received no responses.

On March 2, the US government imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army and its commanders for their role in the capture and occupation of Uvira.

The M23, first formed in 2012 as a rebellion against the Congolese government, reemerged in late 2021 with support from Rwanda. payload.title: Ihmisoikeusjärjestö: Uviran valtauksen jälkeen teloitettiin siviilejä ja tehtiin raiskauksia
payload.summary: Human Rights Watchin selvityksen mukaan M23-kapinalliset ja ruandalaiset sotilaat syyllistyivät vakaviin väkivallantekoihin Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosassa sijaitsevassa Uvirassa kaupungin valtauksen jälkeen.
payload.content:
Human Rights Watchin selvityksen mukaan M23-kapinallisryhmän taistelijat ja ruandalaiset sotilaat syyllistyivät summittaisiin teloituksiin ja raiskauksiin vallattuaan Uviran kaupungin Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosassa joulukuussa. Tanganyikajärven rannalla sijaitseva kaupunki oli ryhmän hallinnassa viikkojen ajan, ja kymmenettuhannet ihmiset pakenivat kodeistaan valtauksen yhteydessä.

## Selvitys kuvaa ovelta ovelle tehtyjä iskuja

Ihmisoikeusjärjestön mukaan sen tutkijat löysivät näyttöä 53 siviilin teloituksesta Uviran asuinalueilla tehdyissä ovelta ovelle -ratsioissa. Uhrien joukossa oli järjestön mukaan 46 miestä, yksi nainen ja kuusi lasta.

Järjestö haastatteli 130 kaupungin asukasta. Yksi haastatelluista kertoi M23-taistelijoiden ampuneen ensin hänen naapurinsa päähän. Toinen kertoi nähneensä neljän perheenjäsenensä kuolevan ja paenneensa itse järvelle, koska häneen ei osunut.

Selvityksessä dokumentoitiin myös kahdeksan raiskaustapausta, joiden väitetään tapahtuneen M23:n ja ruandalaisten sotilaiden miehityksen aikana. Osa haastatelluista kertoi nähneensä väkivallantekoja, joihin heidän mukaansa osallistuivat sekä M23-taistelijat että Ruandan univormuihin pukeutuneet sotilaat.

## Rwanda kiistää tukensa M23:lle

Rwanda on johdonmukaisesti kiistänyt tukevansa M23-ryhmää tai sijoittaneensa omia sotilaitaan Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosiin. M23 ja Ruandan hallitus eivät olleet vastanneet BBC:n kommenttipyyntöön lähdeaineiston mukaan.

Yhdysvallat ja Euroopan maat ovat syyttäneet Ruandaa kapinallishyökkäyksen tukemisesta. Myös YK:n asiantuntijat ovat väittäneet Ruandalla olevan tosiasiallinen määräysvalta M23:n operaatioihin. Heidän mukaansa M23:n värvättyjä on koulutettu Ruandan valvonnassa ja ryhmää on tuettu ruandalaisella korkean teknologian aseistuksella.

## Vetäytyminen seurasi diplomaattista painetta

M23 valtasi Uviran vain päiviä sen jälkeen, kun Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump oli välittänyt rauhansopimusta Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan presidentin Felix Tshisekedin ja Ruandan presidentin Paul Kagamen välillä. Sopimuksella pyrittiin lopettamaan tuhoisa konflikti luonnonvaroiltaan rikkaalla alueella.

Uvira sijaitsee lähellä Burundin rajaa ja toimii porttina Burundiin, joka on Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan tärkeä sotilaallinen liittolainen. M23 vetäytyi kaupungista tammikuussa voimakkaan diplomaattisen painostuksen jälkeen. HRW:n raporttia kuvataan ensimmäiseksi yksityiskohtaiseksi selvitykseksi siitä, mitä Uvirassa tapahtui M23:n hallinnan aikana.
summary_bullets: Human Rights Watchin mukaan Uvirassa teloitettiin 53 siviiliä M23:n valtauksen jälkeen.
Järjestö dokumentoi myös kahdeksan raiskaustapausta miehityksen ajalta.
Rwanda kiistää tukensa M23:lle, vaikka länsimaat ja YK:n asiantuntijat ovat syyttäneet sitä ryhmän tukemisesta.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olevaan BBC:n koostamaan aineistoon ja Human Rights Watchin selvityksestä raportoituihin tietoihin. Väitteet Ruandan ja M23:n osallisuudesta on esitetty syytöksinä, koska osapuolet kiistävät tai eivät ole kommentoineet niitä.

Rwanda kiistää tukensa M23:lle, vaikka länsimaat ja YK:n asiantuntijat ovat syyttäneet sitä ryhmän tukemisesta.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olevaan BBC:n koostamaan aineistoon ja Human Rights Watchin selvityksestä raportoituihin tietoihin. Väitteet Ruandan ja M23:n osallisuudesta on esitetty syytöksinä, koska osapuolet kiistävät tai eivät ole kommentoineet niitä.
article.source_text:
Rebel fighters and Rwandan troops are accused of committing atrocities after capturing the DR Congo city of Uvira in December.

Summary executions and rape were among the atrocities committed by the M23 rebel group and Rwandan soldiers during their weeks-long occupation of the lakeside city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, an investigation by a leading rights group has found. Human Rights Watch (HRW) says its investigators found evidence of the execution of 53 civilians - 46 men, one woman and six children - during door-to-door raids in the city's neighbourhoods after the rebels, widely believed to be backed by Rwanda, captured it in December. Rwanda has consistently denied that it supports that M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to resource-rich eastern DR Congo. But HRW says many of the interviewees alleged witnessing atrocities committed by uniformed Rwandan soldiers as well as M23 fighters.

"They [M23 fighters] shot my neighbour first in the head," said one of the 130 residents interviewed by HRW. Another said he saw four members of his family killed. "I wasn't hit so I just ran to the lake. I saw my brother, his wife, and two of his children fall," he was quoted as saying. The M23 and Rwandan government have not yet responded to a BBC request for comment. Warning: This article contains descriptions of sexual violence The M23 captured Uvira - which lies on the shores of Lake Tanganyika - days after US President Donald Trump brokered a peace deal between DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi and his Rwandan counterpart Paul Kagame in a bid to end the devastating conflict in the resource-rich region.

The US and European powers accuse Rwanda - which borders eastern DR Congo - of supporting the rebel offensive. UN experts have accused Rwanda of having "de facto control" of the M23's operations. They said M23 recruits were trained under Rwandan supervision and supported by high-tech Rwandan weaponry. The M23 withdrew from Uvira - the gateway to Burundi, a key military ally of DR Congo - in January following intense diplomatic pressure. The HRW report is the first detailed study of what happened in the city when it was under M23 control. Tens of thousands of people fled their homes when the group seized control of it. HRW says it documented eight cases of rape allegedly committed by the rebels and Rwandan soldiers during the occupation.
